Subject: Re: Opal - request for tighter p95 & uptime commitment

Lauren / team — quick technical readout:

Short answer: achievable with constraints.

What we need:
- Dedicated reserved pool (N GPUs) pinned to Opal’s traffic; no multi-tenant sharing during peak.
- Priority queueing and pre-warmed KV cache for common prefixes in their workload.
- Model variant: use the quantized 8-bit xq model variant (verified at 90–95ms p95 on A100 80GB with our continuous batching disabled for tail-sensitive paths).
- Probe + synthetic traffic plus adaptive warmers to prevent cold-start tails.

Operational caveats / runbook asks:
- 24/7 paging for P1 infra ops with a runbook for failover to regional fallback model (results in higher latency but keeps availability).
- Additional SLI: cold-start rate and queue-saturation percentage — if either crosses thresholds we trigger temporary rate-limiting or a fallback gray route.

Risk: under unexpected traffic spikes, meeting 90ms p95 requires strict admission controls which can translate to higher error/latency for non-critical requests unless we accept higher reserved capacity.

Preliminary resource estimate: +30–55% monthly committed cost depending on target headroom (I/O bound vs compute bound). I’ll attach a short snippet of required runbook changes.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prod-runbook-snippet.txt (runbook excerpt)

Subject: Re: Opal - request for tighter p95 & uptime commitment

Thanks Marcus — useful details. From product/offer perspective:

Proposal (tradeoff-focused):
- Offer: "Dedicated Performance SLO" — p95 <= 95ms standard, with an optional paid "Commitment Tier" for p95 <= 90ms conditioned on (1) 12-month reserved capacity, (2) front-door admission policy, and (3) agreed synthetic probe profile.
- SLA clause: exclude measured degradation caused by customer-side pattern changes >30% from baseline, and provide a remediation credit ladder rather than hard penalties for the first contract year.

Pricing: recommend starting at +40% uplift on their committed spend for the 90ms guaranteed tier, with an option for monthly True-Up based on observed QPS. Finance/commercial can refine.

Next steps for Sales: get Opal to sign a mutual action plan, accept the probe profile, and agree to a pilot month with agreed-upon traffic that we can use to tune warmers.

Happy to help draft the SLO wording.

—Aditya Rao
Director, Product
Redwood Inference

Maya / Tom — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment complete; summary and proposed path below.

Summary of what Redwood can offer for Opal Systems:
- Dedicated Performance SLO option: p95 <= 90ms (committed tier) with 99.98% availability.
- Preconditions: 12-month reserved capacity commitment (N GPUs), agreed synthetic probe profile and warming plan, and a small initial pilot month to validate traffic shape.
- Controls: priority queueing, pre-warmed caches, and a regional fallback that preserves availability but may exceed 90ms p95 during severe events.
- Monitoring: we will surface cold-start rate and queue saturation as SLIs; remediation credit ladder (first year: credits up to X% of monthly committed spend; product/legal to finalize language).
- Estimated uplift: ~+40% on committed monthly spend (Aditya / Finance to provide final quote).

Attachments: opal_sla_proposal_v1.pdf (detailed wording draft), cost_impact_estimate_q3.csv (first-pass uplift numbers).

Requested next steps from Opal:
1) Confirm appetite for 12-month reserved commitment and pilot month.
2) Share final traffic profile and approve the synthetic probe profile (I’ve attached our suggested probe).
3) If accepted, I’ll loop in Contracts to draft the clause and route for legal review.

If this looks good, Tom — can you confirm procurement timeline? We aim to have draft contract with SLO wording to you by next Wednesday.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
